name: Yale University Press (books)
description: Book manuscripts for Yale University Press: endnotes numbered anew in each chapter, subheads used sparingly and never numbered, quotations set off as a block only from 100 words, and Chicago notes and bibliography.

source.name: Yale University Press, Manuscript Preparation Guidelines (with Preparing Your Manuscript Files and PDFs, and Assembling Notes and Documentation)
source.notes: The Press asks for structure, not appearance. Not specified for ordinary manuscripts, and taken from the general default: margins, typeface and size (a Unicode font where special characters occur), line spacing, paragraph style, alignment, hyphenation, the typographic form of headings (Word's Heading 1, 2 and 3 for A, B and C heads, in title-style capitals), the indent of block quotations, size and spacing of notes, layout of the bibliography, page numbers, running head, abstract and keywords. The page size is not stated: letter was chosen for a North American publisher. The source runs in quotations 'of fewer than 100 words' and sets off those 'longer than 100 words'; from 100 is entered. Footnotes are generally not used. A half-title page and a title page open the manuscript. A bibliography is optional where the notes give full citations. The Press prefers the notes and bibliography system of the Chicago Manual, 18th ed. No ibid., op. cit., supra or infra; no bold or underlining for emphasis; no cross-references to pages. Word (preferred) or RTF, with a PDF of every file.

requirements.note: Length and the number of illustrations are as the contract stipulates.
